items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Haywood Henry was in this band... 'Bama State Collegians was the first one... Haywood joined us. That made the fourth sax.

ctx.x: Okay. What was that band like?

Jazz. Jazz. And it was like, this was the band that had Dud Bascomb in. Jimmy Mitchelle was in it. Bob Range was in this band. All of us. Haywood Henry was in this band, and a few others. I can't think of the rest of the boys.
But, it was second band. 'Bama State Collegians was the first one. So, most of the fellows were finishing out at 'Bama the next year.

items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: In the last couple of years, like Richard Harris, Heywood Henry, Sammy Lowe, Bobby Johnson... We see each other every now and then.

ctx.x: Well, it was a beautiful time of being together. I'll never forget it. And when we started losing one another, it was kind of hard. And then, when the band broke down to small pieces, and we found out this person was gone, we didn't know how to take it.
But right now, those that are left, we still call each other at times. In the last couple of years, like Richard Harris, Heywood Henry, Sammy Lowe, Bobby Johnson. Another name or two may come up.

We see each other every now and then. I was by Sam Lowe's house two days ago. He was really expecting me. I was in Teaneck. I went by to see my accountant. I had a little time to spend. I went and knocked on his door. He was surprised. Hawk, what you doing around here!
